title: Phase 0: Evaluation Harness
goal: Build a reproducible evaluation harness before any serious training work begins.
summary: Phase 0 creates the measurement layer for the lab: task schemas, repeatable suites, backend adapters, Ollama baselines, reports, and reading notes about what makes an eval useful or misleading.

tasks.title: Environment and repo setup
tasks.why: The conda environment, GPU stack, Ollama API, paper library, and git repo give every later experiment a stable base.

tasks.title: Evaluation schema and suite loader
tasks.why: Stable task records make it possible to compare runs without quietly changing what was measured.

tasks.title: Scoring, runner, and reports
tasks.why: The harness needs objective checks, saved records, and human-readable summaries before model comparisons are trustworthy.

tasks.title: Qwen Ollama baselines
tasks.why: Running the same suite against qwen3.6:27b and qwen3.6:35b gives the first real signal that the harness works on local models.

tasks.title: Evaluation reading notes
tasks.why: The papers explain why eval design is as much about failure modes, coverage, and interpretation as it is about scores.

tasks.title: Microlab Console
tasks.why: The dashboard keeps plans, papers, and future eval evidence visible in one place while the project grows.

title: Phase 1: Data and Tokenization
goal: Build the corpus, filtering, splitting, contamination checks, and tokenizer experiments.
summary: This phase turns raw text into controlled training data and makes tokenization choices visible.

title: Phase 2: Tiny GPT Pretraining
goal: Train a tiny decoder-only transformer from scratch and understand every moving part.
summary: This phase favors small models and transparent training loops over raw model quality.

title: Phase 3: Architecture Ablations
goal: Change one architectural decision at a time and measure loss, throughput, and behavior.
summary: This phase turns transformer implementation details into concrete tradeoffs.

title: Phase 4: Scaling Experiments
goal: Train a small family of models to see scaling behavior on one GPU.
summary: This phase builds intuition about parameter count, token budget, throughput, and bottlenecks.

title: Phase 5: Continued Pretraining
goal: Continue training an open base model on a domain corpus and measure adaptation versus forgetting.
summary: This phase connects from-scratch understanding to practical lab workflows.

title: Phase 6: Supervised Fine-Tuning
goal: Create instruction data and train a chat-style model.
summary: This phase focuses on chat templates, instruction data quality, and before/after behavior.

title: Phase 7: Efficient Fine-Tuning
goal: Use LoRA and QLoRA to adapt larger models on the RTX 6000.
summary: This phase makes memory, quantization, adapter rank, and target modules concrete.

title: Phase 8: Preference Data and Reward Models
goal: Build preference pairs, train a reward model, and inspect its failures.
summary: This phase shows where reward modeling helps and where it can mislead.

title: Phase 9: Offline Preference Optimization
goal: Train with DPO-style methods and compare against SFT on the same evals.
summary: This phase studies how preference optimization changes helpfulness, verbosity, and style.
